title: What If a Country Lost Its Vultures? India Did. 500,000 People Died

scenes.text: What if a country lost its vultures? India did. The birds weren't the only ones to die.
In the early 1990s, India had around 50 million vultures. They were the cleanup crew for the country's dead livestock.
In 1994, a cheap painkiller for cattle called diclofenac arrived. Vultures that fed on treated carcasses died of kidney failure.
Within about a decade, 50 million birds had fallen to a few thousand.
Carcasses rotted in the open. Feral dogs multiplied and spread rabies, and bacteria washed into drinking water.
A 2024 study counted the cost: about 100,000 extra human deaths a year, half a million between 2000 and 2005.

description:
What if a country lost almost all of its vultures?
India did. The country had an estimated 50 million vultures until the veterinary painkiller diclofenac came into wide use in 1994. Vultures that ate the carcasses of treated cattle died of kidney failure, and within about a decade the population had collapsed to a few thousand birds; white-rumped vultures fell by 98 percent, Indian vultures by 95 percent and red-headed vultures by 91 percent. With no vultures to clear them, carcasses rotted in the open, feral dog numbers rose and spread rabies, and bacteria contaminated water. A study by economists Eyal Frank and Anant Sudarshan in the American Economic Review (2024) estimated that death rates rose by more than 4 percent in affected districts, about 100,000 additional human deaths a year and roughly half a million between 2000 and 2005, at a cost of about 69 billion dollars a year. India banned veterinary diclofenac in 2006.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The ban on the drug for animals came in 2006, after most of the birds were gone. Which animal do you think we would miss the most?
